imageAlt: A sample check with numbered callouts.

hotspots.title: 1. Address Field
bullets: Contains the account holder's name and address.
May also include phone number and email address.
Located in the top-left corner of the check.

hotspots.title: 2. Bank Information
bullets: Lists the bank name, city, state, or phone number.
May include the bank's website and branch information.
Can also be located above the memo field.

hotspots.title: 3. Check Number
bullets: A unique identification number for this specific check.
Used for tracking and security.
Appears at the top right (shown here as 101).

hotspots.title: 4. Pay to the Order of
bullets: Specifies the person or company receiving the payment.
Only the named recipient can cash or deposit the check.

hotspots.title: 5. Amount (Numbers)
bullets: The check amount written numerically in figures.
Example: '$100.00' is written in the designated box.

hotspots.title: 6. Amount (Words)
bullets: The check amount written fully in words.
Example: 'One Hundred and 00/100'.
Banks use the written words to confirm the correct value if there is a mismatch with numerical figures.
Often a line is drawn to the word 'Dollars' to prevent unauthorized changes.

hotspots.title: 7. Memo / For
bullets: An optional line to note the purpose of the payment.
Useful for reference numbers (e.g., account or invoice details).
Not used or read by the bank for processing.

hotspots.title: 8. Payer Signature
bullets: The signature of the account holder authorizing the transaction.
A check is invalid and cannot be processed without a signature.

hotspots.title: 9. Routing Number
bullets: A 9-digit code identifying the bank that issued the check.
Found on the bottom-left inside the machine-readable MICR line.
Used for setting up direct deposit and electronic payments.

hotspots.title: 10. Account Number
bullets: Identifies the specific checking account the money is drawn from.
Found in the middle of the MICR line at the bottom.

hotspots.title: 11. Fraction Code
bullets: An alternative representation of the routing and bank code.
Printed as a fraction in the upper right.
Used as a backup if the bottom MICR line is unreadable.

hotspots.title: 12. Date Field
bullets: The date (month/day/year) the check is written and becomes valid.
